comparator.name: English Language and Culture
comparator.route: Balanced literature, linguistics and global-culture elective route
comparator.sourceNotes: The September 2026 redesign has a fixed 60-EC first year; a 60-EC second year combining three compulsory 10-EC courses, the 10-EC Global Change IMPACT choice and four balanced 5-EC literature, linguistics and professional-English electives; and a 60-EC third year with a 30-EC minor, four further balanced electives and a 10-EC BA thesis. This route retains the generic degree’s broad literature, language and Anglophone-culture identity and is selected independently of UCR fit.

comparatorRouteSelection.basis: The generic target has extensive elective choice but no named specialisation. A balanced current route is instantiated by combining literature, linguistics, professional English and the broad Global Change IMPACT course, preserving the programme’s published identity more faithfully than a single-subfield route. The choice is independent of UCR fit.

alternativeSelection.assessment: After the balanced closest match, two generator-backed and feasible directions remain materially distinct: literature, culture and media; and language, rhetoric and cognition. Both meet the pairwise distinctness threshold, so the maximum of three alternatives is reached.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Matched explicitly after semantic review: Understanding English Literatures corresponds to Introduction to Literary Studies.
Great Literary Works includes historically influential literature and provides the closest broad UCR counterpart to the dedicated medieval survey.
Matched explicitly after semantic review: World Literatures in English corresponds to World Myth & Literature.
Both analyse how narratives construct personal and cultural identities.
Film & Text studies adaptation and transformation across literary and audiovisual forms.
Matched explicitly after semantic review: Perspectives: Literary Theories corresponds to Perspectives on Literary Meaning.
Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: no scheduled UCR course was judged a sufficiently direct counterpart to Flux: Literature in the Long 20th Century.
Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: no scheduled UCR course was judged a sufficiently direct counterpart to Strangers: The Alien World of Early Modern Literature.
Style & Meaning studies how linguistic choices produce meaning in social and textual contexts.
Psycholinguistics supplies the closest UCR study of cognitive language processing and development.
Matched explicitly after semantic review: Professional English 1 corresponds to The Art of Rhetorical Communication.
Rhetoric in Action develops argumentation, debate and applied rhetorical performance.
Persuasive Communication advances professional, audience-aware argument and presentation.
Creative Communication Laboratory examines meaning-making in communicative practice, while not replacing formal interactional linguistics.
Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: no scheduled UCR course was judged a sufficiently direct counterpart to English Linguistics: Sociolinguistics Laboratory.
Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: no scheduled UCR course was judged a sufficiently direct counterpart to English Linguistics: Learning and Teaching English.
Both examine how mediated stories shape social identities and cultural understanding.
Media & the Environment directly studies a major global-change issue through cultural representation and public debate.
Advanced Research Seminar develops independent evidence synthesis and research practice closest to the methodological side of a bachelor thesis, without claiming an English-specific dissertation.
Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: no scheduled UCR course was judged a sufficiently direct counterpart to Minor.

notes.text: Groningen offers a dedicated English degree with sequenced English linguistics, English literary history, Professional English and a subject-specific thesis. UCR can construct related liberal-arts pathways from literature, communication, media, history, culture and cognition, but does not reproduce that dedicated sequence or guarantee the same depth in English linguistics and English literary history.
